# version_compare - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/version-compare/0.2.1/target-redirect/version_compare/

## Expand description

Rust library to easily compare version numbers with no specific format, and test against various comparison operators.

Comparing version numbers is hard, especially with weird version number formats.

This library helps you to easily compare any kind of version number with no
specific format using a best-effort approach.
Two version numbers can be compared to each other to get a comparison operator
(`<`, `==`, `>`), or test them against a comparison operator.

Along with version comparison, the library provides various other tools for working with version numbers.

Inspired by PHPs [version_compare()](http://php.net/manual/en/function.version-compare.php).

[§](https://docs.rs#formats)Formats

Version numbers that would parse successfully include:

`1`, `3.10.4.1`, `1.2.alpha`, `1.2.dev.4`, ` `, ` .   -32 . 1`, `MyApp 3.2.0 / build 0932` …

See a list of how version numbers compare [here](https://github.com/timvisee/version-compare/blob/411ed7135741ed7cf2fcf4919012fb5412dc122b/src/test.rs#L50-L103).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use version_compare::{compare, compare_to, Cmp, Version};
let a = "1.2";
let b = "1.5.1";
// The following comparison operators are used:
// - Cmp::Eq -> Equal
// - Cmp::Ne -> Not equal
// - Cmp::Lt -> Less than
// - Cmp::Le -> Less than or equal
// - Cmp::Ge -> Greater than or equal
// - Cmp::Gt -> Greater than
// Easily compare version strings
assert_eq!(compare(a, b), Ok(Cmp::Lt));
assert_eq!(compare_to(a, b, Cmp::Le), Ok(true));
assert_eq!(compare_to(a, b, Cmp::Gt), Ok(false));
// Parse and wrap version strings as a Version
let a = Version::from(a).unwrap();
let b = Version::from(b).unwrap();
// The Version can easily be compared with
assert_eq!(a < b, true);
assert_eq!(a <= b, true);
assert_eq!(a > b, false);
assert_eq!(a != b, true);
assert_eq!(a.compare(&b), Cmp::Lt);
assert_eq!(a.compare_to(&b, Cmp::Lt), true);
// Or match the comparison operators
match a.compare(b) {
    Cmp::Lt => println!("Version a is less than b"),
    Cmp::Eq => println!("Version a is equal to b"),
    Cmp::Gt => println!("Version a is greater than b"),
    _ => unreachable!(),
}
```
See the [ examples](https://github.com/timvisee/version-compare/tree/master/examples) directory for more.

[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

- Compare version numbers, get: `<`,`==`,`>`
- Compare against a comparison operator
(`<`,`<=`,`==`,`!=`,`>=`,`>`)
- Parse complex and unspecified formats
- Static, standalone methods to easily compare version strings in a single line of code

[§](https://docs.rs#semver)Semver

Version numbers using the [semver](http://semver.org/) format are compared
correctly with no additional configuration.

If your version number strings follow this exact format you may be better off
using the [ semver](https://crates.io/crates/semver) crate for more format
specific features.

If that isn’t certain however, `version-compare` makes comparing a breeze.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Manifest](https://docs.rs/struct.Manifest.html)
- Version manifest (configuration).
- [Version](https://docs.rs/struct.Version.html)
- Version struct, wrapping a string, providing useful comparison functions.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [compare](https://docs.rs/fn.compare.html)
- Compare two version number strings to each other.
- [compare_](https://docs.rs/fn.compare_to.html)- to
- Compare two version number strings to each other and test against the given comparison
`operator`.

- Compare two version number strings to each other.
- [compare_](https://docs.rs/fn.compare_to.html)- to
- Compare two version number strings to each other and test against the given comparison
`operator`.

# lib.rs - source

Source: https://docs.rs/version-compare/0.2.1/src/version_compare/lib.rs.html

# version_compare/lib.rs

[1](https://docs.rs#1)//! Rust library to easily compare version numbers with no specific format, and test against various comparison operators.
[2](https://docs.rs#2)//!
[3](https://docs.rs#3)//! Comparing version numbers is hard, especially with weird version number formats.
[4](https://docs.rs#4)//!
[5](https://docs.rs#5)//! This library helps you to easily compare any kind of version number with no
[6](https://docs.rs#6)//! specific format using a best-effort approach.
[7](https://docs.rs#7)//! Two version numbers can be compared to each other to get a comparison operator
[8](https://docs.rs#8)//! (`<`, `==`, `>`), or test them against a comparison operator.
[9](https://docs.rs#9)//!
[10](https://docs.rs#10)//! Along with version comparison, the library provides various other tools for
[11](https://docs.rs#11)//! working with version numbers.
[12](https://docs.rs#12)//!
[13](https://docs.rs#13)//! Inspired by PHPs [version_compare()](http://php.net/manual/en/function.version-compare.php).
[14](https://docs.rs#14)//!
[15](https://docs.rs#15)//! ### Formats
[16](https://docs.rs#16)//!
[17](https://docs.rs#17)//! Version numbers that would parse successfully include:
[18](https://docs.rs#18)//! `1`, `3.10.4.1`, `1.2.alpha`, `1.2.dev.4`, ` `, ` .   -32 . 1`, `MyApp 3.2.0 / build 0932` ...
[19](https://docs.rs#19)//!
[20](https://docs.rs#20)//! See a list of how version numbers compare [here](https://github.com/timvisee/version-compare/blob/411ed7135741ed7cf2fcf4919012fb5412dc122b/src/test.rs#L50-L103).
[21](https://docs.rs#21)//!
[22](https://docs.rs#22)//! ## Examples
[23](https://docs.rs#23)//!
[24](https://docs.rs#24)//! [example.rs](examples/example.rs):
[25](https://docs.rs#25)//! ```rust
[26](https://docs.rs#26)//! use version_compare::{compare, compare_to, Cmp, Version};
[27](https://docs.rs#27)//!
[28](https://docs.rs#28)//! let a = "1.2";
[29](https://docs.rs#29)//! let b = "1.5.1";
[30](https://docs.rs#30)//!
[31](https://docs.rs#31)//! // The following comparison operators are used:
[32](https://docs.rs#32)//! // - Cmp::Eq -> Equal
[33](https://docs.rs#33)//! // - Cmp::Ne -> Not equal
[34](https://docs.rs#34)//! // - Cmp::Lt -> Less than
[35](https://docs.rs#35)//! // - Cmp::Le -> Less than or equal
[36](https://docs.rs#36)//! // - Cmp::Ge -> Greater than or equal
[37](https://docs.rs#37)//! // - Cmp::Gt -> Greater than
[38](https://docs.rs#38)//!
[39](https://docs.rs#39)//! // Easily compare version strings
[40](https://docs.rs#40)//! assert_eq!(compare(a, b), Ok(Cmp::Lt));
[41](https://docs.rs#41)//! assert_eq!(compare_to(a, b, Cmp::Le), Ok(true));
[42](https://docs.rs#42)//! assert_eq!(compare_to(a, b, Cmp::Gt), Ok(false));
[43](https://docs.rs#43)//!
[44](https://docs.rs#44)//! // Parse and wrap version strings as a Version
[45](https://docs.rs#45)//! let a = Version::from(a).unwrap();
[46](https://docs.rs#46)//! let b = Version::from(b).unwrap();
[47](https://docs.rs#47)//!
[48](https://docs.rs#48)//! // The Version can easily be compared with
[49](https://docs.rs#49)//! assert_eq!(a < b, true);
[50](https://docs.rs#50)//! assert_eq!(a <= b, true);
[51](https://docs.rs#51)//! assert_eq!(a > b, false);
[52](https://docs.rs#52)//! assert_eq!(a != b, true);
[53](https://docs.rs#53)//! assert_eq!(a.compare(&b), Cmp::Lt);
[54](https://docs.rs#54)//! assert_eq!(a.compare_to(&b, Cmp::Lt), true);
[55](https://docs.rs#55)//!
[56](https://docs.rs#56)//! // Or match the comparison operators
[57](https://docs.rs#57)//! match a.compare(b) {
[58](https://docs.rs#58)//!     Cmp::Lt => println!("Version a is less than b"),
[59](https://docs.rs#59)//!     Cmp::Eq => println!("Version a is equal to b"),
[60](https://docs.rs#60)//!     Cmp::Gt => println!("Version a is greater than b"),
[61](https://docs.rs#61)//!     _ => unreachable!(),
[62](https://docs.rs#62)//! }
[63](https://docs.rs#63)//! ```
[64](https://docs.rs#64)//!
[65](https://docs.rs#65)//! See the [`examples`](https://github.com/timvisee/version-compare/tree/master/examples) directory for more.
[66](https://docs.rs#66)//!
[67](https://docs.rs#67)//! ## Features
[68](https://docs.rs#68)//!
[69](https://docs.rs#69)//! * Compare version numbers, get: `<`, `==`, `>`
[70](https://docs.rs#70)//! * Compare against a comparison operator
[71](https://docs.rs#71)//!   (`<`, `<=`, `==`, `!=`, `>=`, `>`)
[72](https://docs.rs#72)//! * Parse complex and unspecified formats
[73](https://docs.rs#73)//! * Static, standalone methods to easily compare version strings in a single line
[74](https://docs.rs#74)//!   of code
[75](https://docs.rs#75)//!
[76](https://docs.rs#76)//! ### Semver
[77](https://docs.rs#77)//!
[78](https://docs.rs#78)//! Version numbers using the [semver](http://semver.org/) format are compared
[79](https://docs.rs#79)//! correctly with no additional configuration.
[80](https://docs.rs#80)//!
[81](https://docs.rs#81)//! If your version number strings follow this exact format you may be better off
[82](https://docs.rs#82)//! using the [`semver`](https://crates.io/crates/semver) crate for more format
[83](https://docs.rs#83)//! specific features.
[84](https://docs.rs#84)//!
[85](https://docs.rs#85)//! If that isn't certain however, `version-compare` makes comparing a breeze.
[86](https://docs.rs#86)//!
[87](https://docs.rs#87)//! _[View complete README](https://github.com/timvisee/version-compare/blob/master/README.md)_
[88](https://docs.rs#88)
[89](https://docs.rs#89)mod cmp;
[90](https://docs.rs#90)mod compare;
[91](https://docs.rs#91)mod manifest;
[92](https://docs.rs#92)mod part;
[93](https://docs.rs#93)mod version;
[94](https://docs.rs#94)
[95](https://docs.rs#95)#[cfg(test)]
[96](https://docs.rs#96)mod test;
[97](https://docs.rs#97)
[98](https://docs.rs#98)// Re-exports
[99](https://docs.rs#99)pub use crate::cmp::Cmp;
[100](https://docs.rs#100)pub use crate::compare::{compare, compare_to};
[101](https://docs.rs#101)pub use crate::manifest::Manifest;
[102](https://docs.rs#102)pub use crate::part::Part;
[103](https://docs.rs#103)pub use crate::version::Version;

# Manifest in version_compare - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/version-compare/0.2.1/version_compare/struct.Manifest.html

```
#[non_exhaustive]pub struct Manifest {
    pub max_depth:
```
[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)>,
    pub ignore_text: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html),
    pub gnu_ordering: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html),
}## Expand description

Version manifest (configuration).

A manifest (configuration) that is used respectively when parsing and comparing version strings.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use version_compare::{Manifest, Version};
// Create manifest with max depth of 2
let mut manifest = Manifest::default();
manifest.max_depth = Some(2);
// Version strings equal with manifest because we compare up-to 2 parts deep
let a = Version::from_manifest("1.0.1", &manifest).unwrap();
let b = Version::from_manifest("1.0.2", &manifest).unwrap();
assert!(a == b);
```
## Fields (Non-exhaustive)[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

## This struct is marked as non-exhaustive

`Struct { .. }` syntax; cannot be matched against without a wildcard `..`; and struct update syntax will not work.[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.max_depth)

`max_depth: `[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)>The maximum depth of a version number.

This specifies the maximum number of parts. There is no limit if `None` is set.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.ignore_text)

`ignore_text: `[bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)Whether to ignore text parts in version strings.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.gnu_ordering)

`gnu_ordering: `[bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)Use GNU sort based ordering.

Enabling this modifies the ordering of numbers with a leading zero to mimick GNUs sort.

Issue: https://github.com/timvisee/version-compare/issues/27

# Version in version_compare - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/version-compare/0.2.1/version_compare/struct.Version.html

`pub struct Version<'a> { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Version struct, wrapping a string, providing useful comparison functions.

A version in string format can be parsed using methods like `Version::from("1.2.3");`,
returning a `Result` with the parse result.

The original version string can be accessed using `version.as_str()`. A `Version` that isn’t
derrived from a version string returns a generated string.

The struct provides many methods for easy comparison and probing.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use version_compare::{Version};
let ver = Version::from("1.2.3").unwrap();
```
## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Create a `Version` instance from a version string.

The version string should be passed to the `version` parameter.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-1)Examples

```
use version_compare::{Cmp, Version};
let a = Version::from("1.2.3").unwrap();
let b = Version::from("1.3.0").unwrap();
assert_eq!(a.compare(b), Cmp::Lt);
```
```
12fn main() {
13    let a = "1.2";
14    let b = "1.5.1";
15
16    // The following comparison operators are used:
17    // - Cmp::Eq -> Equal
18    // - Cmp::Ne -> Not equal
19    // - Cmp::Lt -> Less than
20    // - Cmp::Le -> Less than or equal
21    // - Cmp::Ge -> Greater than or equal
22    // - Cmp::Gt -> Greater than
23
24    // Easily compare version strings
25    assert_eq!(compare(a, b), Ok(Cmp::Lt));
26    assert_eq!(compare_to(a, b, Cmp::Le), Ok(true));
27    assert_eq!(compare_to(a, b, Cmp::Gt), Ok(false));
28
29    // Parse and wrap version strings as a Version
30    let a = Version::from(a).unwrap();
31    let b = Version::from(b).unwrap();
32
33    // The Version can easily be compared with
34    assert_eq!(a < b, true);
35    assert_eq!(a <= b, true);
36    assert_eq!(a > b, false);
37    assert_eq!(a != b, true);
38    assert_eq!(a.compare(&b), Cmp::Lt);
39    assert_eq!(a.compare_to(&b, Cmp::Lt), true);
40
41    // Or match the comparison operators
42    match a.compare(b) {
43        Cmp::Lt => println!("Version a is less than b"),
44        Cmp::Eq => println!("Version a is equal to b"),
45        Cmp::Gt => println!("Version a is greater than b"),
46        _ => unreachable!(),
47    }
48}
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/version_compare/version.rs.html#94-100)#### pub fn [from_manifest](https://docs.rs#method.from_manifest)(version: &'a [str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html), manifest: &'a [Manifest](https://docs.rs/struct.Manifest.html)) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<Self>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/version_compare/version.rs.html#94-100)

#### pub fn [from_manifest](https://docs.rs#method.from_manifest)(version: &'a [str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html), manifest: &'a [Manifest](https://docs.rs/struct.Manifest.html)) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<Self>

Create a `Version` instance from a version string with the given `manifest`.

The version string should be passed to the `version` parameter.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-3)Examples

```
use version_compare::{Cmp, Version, Manifest};
let manifest = Manifest::default();
let ver = Version::from_manifest("1.2.3", &manifest).unwrap();
assert_eq!(ver.compare(Version::from("1.2.3").unwrap()), Cmp::Eq);
```
Get the version manifest, if available.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-4)Examples

```
use version_compare::Version;
let version = Version::from("1.2.3").unwrap();
if version.has_manifest() {
    println!(
        "Maximum version part depth is {} for this version",
        version.manifest().unwrap().max_depth.unwrap_or(0),
    );
} else {
    println!("Version has no manifest");
}
```

#### pub fn [set_manifest](https://docs.rs#method.set_manifest)(&mut self, manifest: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&'a [Manifest](https://docs.rs/struct.Manifest.html)>)

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-6)Examples

use version_compare::{Version, Manifest};
let manifest = Manifest::default();
let mut version = Version::from("1.2.3").unwrap();
version.set_manifest(Some(&manifest));
```
Get a specific version part by it’s `index`.
An error is returned if the given index is out of bound.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-8)Examples

```
use version_compare::{Version, Part};
let ver = Version::from("1.2.3").unwrap();
assert_eq!(ver.part(0), Ok(Part::Number(1)));
assert_eq!(ver.part(1), Ok(Part::Number(2)));
assert_eq!(ver.part(2), Ok(Part::Number(3)));
```
Get a vector of all version parts.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-9)Examples

```
use version_compare::{Version, Part};
let ver = Version::from("1.2.3").unwrap();
assert_eq!(ver.parts(), [
    Part::Number(1),
    Part::Number(2),
    Part::Number(3)
]);
```
Compare this version to the given `other` version using the default `Manifest`.

This method returns one of the following comparison operators:

- `Lt`
- `Eq`
- `Gt`

Other comparison operators can be used when comparing, but aren’t returned by this method.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-10)Examples:

```
use version_compare::{Cmp, Version};
let a = Version::from("1.2").unwrap();
let b = Version::from("1.3.2").unwrap();
assert_eq!(a.compare(&b), Cmp::Lt);
assert_eq!(b.compare(&a), Cmp::Gt);
assert_eq!(a.compare(&a), Cmp::Eq);
```
```
12fn main() {
13    let a = "1.2";
14    let b = "1.5.1";
15
16    // The following comparison operators are used:
17    // - Cmp::Eq -> Equal
18    // - Cmp::Ne -> Not equal
19    // - Cmp::Lt -> Less than
20    // - Cmp::Le -> Less than or equal
21    // - Cmp::Ge -> Greater than or equal
22    // - Cmp::Gt -> Greater than
23
24    // Easily compare version strings
25    assert_eq!(compare(a, b), Ok(Cmp::Lt));
26    assert_eq!(compare_to(a, b, Cmp::Le), Ok(true));
27    assert_eq!(compare_to(a, b, Cmp::Gt), Ok(false));
28
29    // Parse and wrap version strings as a Version
30    let a = Version::from(a).unwrap();
31    let b = Version::from(b).unwrap();
32
33    // The Version can easily be compared with
34    assert_eq!(a < b, true);
35    assert_eq!(a <= b, true);
36    assert_eq!(a > b, false);
37    assert_eq!(a != b, true);
38    assert_eq!(a.compare(&b), Cmp::Lt);
39    assert_eq!(a.compare_to(&b, Cmp::Lt), true);
40
41    // Or match the comparison operators
42    match a.compare(b) {
43        Cmp::Lt => println!("Version a is less than b"),
44        Cmp::Eq => println!("Version a is equal to b"),
45        Cmp::Gt => println!("Version a is greater than b"),
46        _ => unreachable!(),
47    }
48}
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/version_compare/version.rs.html#270-280)#### pub fn [compare_to](https://docs.rs#method.compare_to)<V>(&self, other: V, operator: [Cmp](https://docs.rs/enum.Cmp.html)) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/version_compare/version.rs.html#270-280)

#### pub fn [compare_to](https://docs.rs#method.compare_to)<V>(&self, other: V, operator: [Cmp](https://docs.rs/enum.Cmp.html)) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

Compare this version to the given `other` version,
and check whether the given comparison operator is valid using the default `Manifest`.

All comparison operators can be used.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-11)Examples:

```
use version_compare::{Cmp, Version};
let a = Version::from("1.2").unwrap();
let b = Version::from("1.3.2").unwrap();
assert!(a.compare_to(&b, Cmp::Lt));
assert!(a.compare_to(&b, Cmp::Le));
assert!(a.compare_to(&a, Cmp::Eq));
assert!(a.compare_to(&a, Cmp::Le));
```
```
12fn main() {
13    let a = "1.2";
14    let b = "1.5.1";
15
16    // The following comparison operators are used:
17    // - Cmp::Eq -> Equal
18    // - Cmp::Ne -> Not equal
19    // - Cmp::Lt -> Less than
20    // - Cmp::Le -> Less than or equal
21    // - Cmp::Ge -> Greater than or equal
22    // - Cmp::Gt -> Greater than
23
24    // Easily compare version strings
25    assert_eq!(compare(a, b), Ok(Cmp::Lt));
26    assert_eq!(compare_to(a, b, Cmp::Le), Ok(true));
27    assert_eq!(compare_to(a, b, Cmp::Gt), Ok(false));
28
29    // Parse and wrap version strings as a Version
30    let a = Version::from(a).unwrap();
31    let b = Version::from(b).unwrap();
32
33    // The Version can easily be compared with
34    assert_eq!(a < b, true);
35    assert_eq!(a <= b, true);
36    assert_eq!(a > b, false);
37    assert_eq!(a != b, true);
38    assert_eq!(a.compare(&b), Cmp::Lt);
39    assert_eq!(a.compare_to(&b, Cmp::Lt), true);
40
41    // Or match the comparison operators
42    match a.compare(b) {
43        Cmp::Lt => println!("Version a is less than b"),
44        Cmp::Eq => println!("Version a is equal to b"),
45        Cmp::Gt => println!("Version a is greater than b"),
46        _ => unreachable!(),
47    }
48}
```

# Cmp in version_compare - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/version-compare/0.2.1/version_compare/enum.Cmp.html

```
pub enum Cmp {
    Eq,
    Ne,
    Lt,
    Le,
    Ge,
    Gt,
}
```
## Expand description

Comparison operators enum.

## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Eq)

### Eq

Equal (`==`, `=`).
When version `A` is equal to `B`.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Ne)

### Ne

Not equal (`!=`, `!`, `<>`).
When version `A` is not equal to `B`.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Lt)

### Lt

Less than (`<`).
When version `A` is less than `B` but not equal.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Le)

### Le

Less or equal (`<=`).
When version `A` is less than or equal to `B`.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Ge)

### Ge

Greater or equal (`>=`).
When version `A` is greater than or equal to `B`.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Gt)

### Gt

Greater than (`>`).
When version `A` is greater than `B` but not equal.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Get a comparison operator by it’s sign. Whitespaces are stripped from the sign string. An error is returned if the sign isn’t recognized.

The following signs are supported:

- `==`- *or*- `=`->- `Eq`
- `!=`- *or*- `!`- *or*- `<>`->- `Ne`
- `<`->- `Lt`
- `<=`->- `Le`
- `>=`->- `Ge`
- `>`->- `Gt`

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use version_compare::Cmp;
assert_eq!(Cmp::from_sign("=="), Ok(Cmp::Eq));
assert_eq!(Cmp::from_sign("<"), Ok(Cmp::Lt));
assert_eq!(Cmp::from_sign("  >=   "), Ok(Cmp::Ge));
assert!(Cmp::from_sign("*").is_err());
```
Get a comparison operator by it’s name. Names are case-insensitive, and whitespaces are stripped from the string. An error is returned if the name isn’t recognized.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-1)Examples

```
use version_compare::Cmp;
assert_eq!(Cmp::from_name("eq"), Ok(Cmp::Eq));
assert_eq!(Cmp::from_name("lt"), Ok(Cmp::Lt));
assert_eq!(Cmp::from_name("  Ge   "), Ok(Cmp::Ge));
assert!(Cmp::from_name("abc").is_err());
```
Get the comparison operator from Rusts `Ordering` enum.

The following comparison operators are returned:

- `Ordering::Less`->- `Lt`
- `Ordering::Equal`->- `Eq`
- `Ordering::Greater`->- `Gt`

Get the inverted comparison operator.

This uses the following bidirectional rules:

- `Eq`<->- `Ne`
- `Lt`<->- `Ge`
- `Le`<->- `Gt`

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-3)Examples

```
use version_compare::Cmp;
assert_eq!(Cmp::Eq.invert(), Cmp::Ne);
assert_eq!(Cmp::Lt.invert(), Cmp::Ge);
assert_eq!(Cmp::Gt.invert(), Cmp::Le);
```
Get the opposite comparison operator.

This uses the following bidirectional rules:

- `Eq`<->- `Ne`
- `Lt`<->- `Gt`
- `Le`<->- `Ge`

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-4)Examples

```
use version_compare::Cmp;
assert_eq!(Cmp::Eq.opposite(), Cmp::Ne);
assert_eq!(Cmp::Lt.opposite(), Cmp::Gt);
assert_eq!(Cmp::Ge.opposite(), Cmp::Le);
```
Get the flipped comparison operator.

This uses the following bidirectional rules:

- `Lt`<->- `Gt`
- `Le`<->- `Ge`
- Other operators are returned as is.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-5)Examples

```
use version_compare::Cmp;
assert_eq!(Cmp::Eq.flip(), Cmp::Eq);
assert_eq!(Cmp::Lt.flip(), Cmp::Gt);
assert_eq!(Cmp::Ge.flip(), Cmp::Le);
```
Get the sign for this comparison operator.

The following signs are returned:

- `Eq`->- `==`
- `Ne`->- `!=`
- `Lt`->- `<`
- `Le`->- `<=`
- `Ge`->- `>=`
- `Gt`->- `>`

Note: Some comparison operators also support other signs,
such as `=` for `Eq` and `!` for `Ne`,
these are never returned by this method however as the table above is used.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-6)Examples

```
use version_compare::Cmp;
assert_eq!(Cmp::Eq.sign(), "==");
assert_eq!(Cmp::Lt.sign(), "<");
assert_eq!(Cmp::Ge.flip().sign(), "<=");
```
Get a factor (number) for this comparison operator. These factors can be useful for quick calculations.

The following factor numbers are returned:

- `Eq`- *or*- `Ne`->- `0`
- `Lt`- *or*- `Le`->- `-1`
- `Gt`- *or*- `Ge`->- `1`

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-7)Examples

```
use version_compare::Version;
let a = Version::from("1.2.3").unwrap();
let b = Version::from("1.3").unwrap();
assert_eq!(a.compare(&b).factor(), -1);
assert_eq!(10 * b.compare(a).factor(), 10);
```
Get Rust’s ordering for this comparison operator.

The following comparison operators are supported:

- `Eq`->- `Ordering::Equal`
- `Lt`->- `Ordering::Less`
- `Gt`->- `Ordering::Greater`

For other comparison operators `None` is returned.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-8)Examples

```
use std::cmp::Ordering;
use version_compare::Version;
let a = Version::from("1.2.3").unwrap();
let b = Version::from("1.3").unwrap();
assert_eq!(a.compare(b).ord().unwrap(), Ordering::Less);
```
## Trait Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#trait-implementations)

# compare in version_compare - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/version-compare/0.2.1/version_compare/fn.compare.html

## Expand description

Compare two version number strings to each other.

This compares version `a` to version `b`, and returns whether version `a` is greater, less
or equal to version `b`.

If either version number string is invalid an error is returned.

One of the following operators is returned:

- `Cmp::Eq`
- `Cmp::Lt`
- `Cmp::Gt`

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use version_compare::{Cmp, compare};
assert_eq!(compare("1.2.3", "1.2.3"), Ok(Cmp::Eq));
assert_eq!(compare("1.2.3", "1.2.4"), Ok(Cmp::Lt));
assert_eq!(compare("1", "0.1"), Ok(Cmp::Gt));
```
## More examples

```
12fn main() {
13    let a = "1.2";
14    let b = "1.5.1";
15
16    // The following comparison operators are used:
17    // - Cmp::Eq -> Equal
18    // - Cmp::Ne -> Not equal
19    // - Cmp::Lt -> Less than
20    // - Cmp::Le -> Less than or equal
21    // - Cmp::Ge -> Greater than or equal
22    // - Cmp::Gt -> Greater than
23
24    // Easily compare version strings
25    assert_eq!(compare(a, b), Ok(Cmp::Lt));
26    assert_eq!(compare_to(a, b, Cmp::Le), Ok(true));
27    assert_eq!(compare_to(a, b, Cmp::Gt), Ok(false));
28
29    // Parse and wrap version strings as a Version
30    let a = Version::from(a).unwrap();
31    let b = Version::from(b).unwrap();
32
33    // The Version can easily be compared with
34    assert_eq!(a < b, true);
35    assert_eq!(a <= b, true);
36    assert_eq!(a > b, false);
37    assert_eq!(a != b, true);
38    assert_eq!(a.compare(&b), Cmp::Lt);
39    assert_eq!(a.compare_to(&b, Cmp::Lt), true);
40
41    // Or match the comparison operators
42    match a.compare(b) {
43        Cmp::Lt => println!("Version a is less than b"),
44        Cmp::Eq => println!("Version a is equal to b"),
45        Cmp::Gt => println!("Version a is greater than b"),
46        _ => unreachable!(),
47    }
48}
```

---

# compare_to in version_compare - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/version-compare/0.2.1/version_compare/fn.compare_to.html

## Expand description

Compare two version number strings to each other and test against the given comparison
`operator`.

If either version number string is invalid an error is returned.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use version_compare::{Cmp, compare_to};
assert!(compare_to("1.2.3", "1.2.3", Cmp::Eq).unwrap());
assert!(compare_to("1.2.3", "1.2.3", Cmp::Le).unwrap());
assert!(compare_to("1.2.3", "1.2.4", Cmp::Lt).unwrap());
assert!(compare_to("1", "0.1", Cmp::Gt).unwrap());
assert!(compare_to("1", "0.1", Cmp::Ge).unwrap());
```
```
12fn main() {
13    let a = "1.2";
14    let b = "1.5.1";
15
16    // The following comparison operators are used:
17    // - Cmp::Eq -> Equal
18    // - Cmp::Ne -> Not equal
19    // - Cmp::Lt -> Less than
20    // - Cmp::Le -> Less than or equal
21    // - Cmp::Ge -> Greater than or equal
22    // - Cmp::Gt -> Greater than
23
24    // Easily compare version strings
25    assert_eq!(compare(a, b), Ok(Cmp::Lt));
26    assert_eq!(compare_to(a, b, Cmp::Le), Ok(true));
27    assert_eq!(compare_to(a, b, Cmp::Gt), Ok(false));
28
29    // Parse and wrap version strings as a Version
30    let a = Version::from(a).unwrap();
31    let b = Version::from(b).unwrap();
32
33    // The Version can easily be compared with
34    assert_eq!(a < b, true);
35    assert_eq!(a <= b, true);
36    assert_eq!(a > b, false);
37    assert_eq!(a != b, true);
38    assert_eq!(a.compare(&b), Cmp::Lt);
39    assert_eq!(a.compare_to(&b, Cmp::Lt), true);
40
41    // Or match the comparison operators
42    match a.compare(b) {
43        Cmp::Lt => println!("Version a is less than b"),
44        Cmp::Eq => println!("Version a is equal to b"),
45        Cmp::Gt => println!("Version a is greater than b"),
46        _ => unreachable!(),
47    }
48}
```

# version_compare - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/version-compare/latest/version_compare/

## Expand description

Rust library to easily compare version numbers with no specific format, and test against various comparison operators.

Comparing version numbers is hard, especially with weird version number formats.

This library helps you to easily compare any kind of version number with no
specific format using a best-effort approach.
Two version numbers can be compared to each other to get a comparison operator
(`<`, `==`, `>`), or test them against a comparison operator.

Along with version comparison, the library provides various other tools for working with version numbers.

Inspired by PHPs [version_compare()](http://php.net/manual/en/function.version-compare.php).

[§](https://docs.rs#formats)Formats

Version numbers that would parse successfully include:

`1`, `3.10.4.1`, `1.2.alpha`, `1.2.dev.4`, ` `, ` .   -32 . 1`, `MyApp 3.2.0 / build 0932` …

See a list of how version numbers compare [here](https://github.com/timvisee/version-compare/blob/411ed7135741ed7cf2fcf4919012fb5412dc122b/src/test.rs#L50-L103).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use version_compare::{compare, compare_to, Cmp, Version};
let a = "1.2";
let b = "1.5.1";
// The following comparison operators are used:
// - Cmp::Eq -> Equal
// - Cmp::Ne -> Not equal
// - Cmp::Lt -> Less than
// - Cmp::Le -> Less than or equal
// - Cmp::Ge -> Greater than or equal
// - Cmp::Gt -> Greater than
// Easily compare version strings
assert_eq!(compare(a, b), Ok(Cmp::Lt));
assert_eq!(compare_to(a, b, Cmp::Le), Ok(true));
assert_eq!(compare_to(a, b, Cmp::Gt), Ok(false));
// Parse and wrap version strings as a Version
let a = Version::from(a).unwrap();
let b = Version::from(b).unwrap();
// The Version can easily be compared with
assert_eq!(a < b, true);
assert_eq!(a <= b, true);
assert_eq!(a > b, false);
assert_eq!(a != b, true);
assert_eq!(a.compare(&b), Cmp::Lt);
assert_eq!(a.compare_to(&b, Cmp::Lt), true);
// Or match the comparison operators
match a.compare(b) {
    Cmp::Lt => println!("Version a is less than b"),
    Cmp::Eq => println!("Version a is equal to b"),
    Cmp::Gt => println!("Version a is greater than b"),
    _ => unreachable!(),
}
```
See the [ examples](https://github.com/timvisee/version-compare/tree/master/examples) directory for more.

[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

- Compare version numbers, get: `<`,`==`,`>`
- Compare against a comparison operator
(`<`,`<=`,`==`,`!=`,`>=`,`>`)
- Parse complex and unspecified formats
- Static, standalone methods to easily compare version strings in a single line of code

[§](https://docs.rs#semver)Semver

Version numbers using the [semver](http://semver.org/) format are compared
correctly with no additional configuration.

If your version number strings follow this exact format you may be better off
using the [ semver](https://crates.io/crates/semver) crate for more format
specific features.

If that isn’t certain however, `version-compare` makes comparing a breeze.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Manifest](https://docs.rs/struct.Manifest.html)
- Version manifest (configuration).
- [Version](https://docs.rs/struct.Version.html)
- Version struct, wrapping a string, providing useful comparison functions.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [compare](https://docs.rs/fn.compare.html)
- Compare two version number strings to each other.
- [compare_](https://docs.rs/fn.compare_to.html)- to
- Compare two version number strings to each other and test against the given comparison
`operator`.

# version-compare 0.2.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/version-compare/0.2.0

# Rust library: version-compare

Rust library to easily compare version numbers with no specific format, and test against various comparison operators.

Comparing version numbers is hard, especially with weird version number formats.

This library helps you to easily compare any kind of version number with no
specific format using a best-effort approach.
Two version numbers can be compared to each other to get a comparison operator
(`<`, `==`, `>`), or test them against a comparison operator.

Along with version comparison, the library provides various other tools for working with version numbers.

Inspired by PHPs [version_compare()](http://php.net/manual/en/function.version-compare.php).

*Note: Still a work in progress. Configurability is currently very limited. Things will change.*

### Formats

Version numbers that would parse successfully include:

`1`, `3.10.4.1`, `1.2.alpha`, `1.2.dev.4`, ` `, ` .   -32 . 1`, `MyApp 3.2.0 / build 0932` ...

See a list of how version numbers compare [here](https://github.com/timvisee/version-compare/blob/411ed7135741ed7cf2fcf4919012fb5412dc122b/src/test.rs#L50-L103).

## Example

This library is very easy to use. Here's a basic usage example:

`Cargo.toml`:

```
[]
 = "0.1"
```
```
use ;
```
See the [ examples](https://docs.rs/examples) directory for more.

## Features

- Compare version numbers, get: `<`,`==`,`>`
- Compare against a comparison operator
(`<`,`<=`,`==`,`!=`,`>=`,`>`)
- Parse complex and unspecified formats
- Static, standalone methods to easily compare version strings in a single line of code

#### Future ideas

- Version ranges
- Support for [npm-style](https://semver.npmjs.com/)operators (e.g.`^1.0`or`~1.0`)
- Manifest: extend `Manifest`for to support a wide set of constraints
- Building blocks for building your own specific version number parser
- Batch comparisons

#### Semver

Version numbers using the [semver](http://semver.org/) format are compared
correctly with no additional configuration.

If your version number strings follow this exact format you may be better off
using the [ semver](https://crates.io/crates/semver) crate for more format
specific features.

If that isn't certain however, `version-compare` makes comparing a breeze.

## Builds

This library is automatically build and tested every day and for each commit using CI services.

See the current status here: [https://gitlab.com/timvisee/version-compare/-/pipelines](https://gitlab.com/timvisee/version-compare/-/pipelines)

## License

This project is released under the MIT license. Check out the [LICENSE](https://docs.rs/LICENSE) file for more information.

# version-compare 0.1.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/version-compare/0.1.0

# Rust library: version-compare

A Rust library to easily compare version numbers in any format, and test them against various comparison operators.

Comparing version numbers is hard. Especially when version numbers get really complex, or when their formatting differs.

This library helps you to easily compare any kind of version number with minimal code.
Two version numbers can be compared to each other, to get a relevant comparison operator (`<`, `==`, `>`),
or version numbers can be tested against any given comparison operator.

Along with version comparison, the library also features other useful tools.

For example: version numbers can be parsed to inspect a version number by it's bare numeric or text based parts.

Inspired by PHPs [version_compare()](http://php.net/manual/en/function.version-compare.php).

**Note:** This library is still a work in progress.
See the list below for a list of currently available and future features.

### Formats

A list of version number examples that are parsed successfully:

- `1`
- `3.10.4.1`
- `1.2.alpha`
- `1.2.dev.4`
- *(empty)*
- `. -32 . 1`- *(undefined formats)*
- `MyApp 3.2.0 / build 0932`- *(complex formats, not fully functional yet)*
- *Many more and support for custom formats to come...*

### Semver

Version number formats like [ semver](http://semver.org/) try to make version numbers consistent and manageable,
there are too many projects however that don't follow such format.

`version-compare` makes working with them easy and supports semver formats out of the box with zero configuration.

## Features

- Compare two version numbers, get: `<`,`==`or`>`.
- Compare two version numbers against a comparison operator
- Parse complex and undefined version number formats.
- Static, standalone methods to easily compare version strings

The following features will be added in a later version:

- Version manifest, to specify detailed version number constraints.
- Version ranges, and tests against them.
- Support for operators in version strings, [npm-style](https://docs.npmjs.com/misc/semver), and tests against them.
- Batch comparisons.

## Example

This library is very easy to use. Here's a basic usage example:

Cargo.toml:

```
[]
 = "0.1"
```
```
use ;
```
Check out the [examples](https://docs.rs/examples) directory for more complete examples.

## Builds

This library is automatically build and tested every day and for each commit using CI services.

See the current status here: [https://gitlab.com/timvisee/version-compare/-/pipelines](https://gitlab.com/timvisee/version-compare/-/pipelines)

## License

This project is released under the MIT license. Check out the [LICENSE](https://docs.rs/LICENSE) file for more information.

Comparing version numbers is hard. Especially when version numbers get really complex, or when their formatting differs.

This library helps you to easily compare any kind of version number with a single code-statement.
Two version numbers can be compared to each other, to get a relevant comparison operator (`<`, `==`, `>`),
or version numbers can be tested against any given comparison operator.

Along with version comparison, the library also features other useful tools.

For example: version numbers can be parsed to inspect a version number by it's bare numeric or text based parts.

Inspired by PHPs [version_compare()](http://php.net/manual/en/function.version-compare.php).

Note: This library is still a work in progress. See the list below for a list of currently available and future features.

## Features

- Compare two version numbers, get: `<`,`==`or`>`.
- Compare two version numbers against any comparison operator.
- Parse complex version numbers.
- Static, single-statement methods available.

The following features will be added in a later version:

- Support for text parts in version strings.
- Version manifest, to specify detailed version number constraints.
- Batch comparisons.

## Example

This library is very easy to use. Here's a basic usage example:

Cargo.toml:

```
[]
 = "0.0.5"
```
```
extern crate version_compare;
use ;
```
Check out the [examples](https://docs.rs/examples) directory for more complete examples.

## Builds

This library is automatically build and tested for each commit using CI services.

| Service | Branch | Build Status | |
|---|---|---|---|
| Travis CI | master | [View Status](https://travis-ci.org/timvisee/version-compare) | |
| Travis CI | last commit | [View Status](https://travis-ci.org/timvisee/version-compare) |

## License

This project is released under the GNU GPL-3.0 license. Check out the [LICENSE](https://docs.rs/LICENSE) file for more information.

# Rust library: version-compare

A Rust library to easily compare version numbers, and test them against various comparison operators.

Comparing version numbers is hard. Especially when version numbers get really complex, or when their formatting differs.

This library helps you to easily compare any kind of version number with a single code-statement.
Two version numbers can be compared to each other, to get a relevant comparison operator (`<`, `==`, `>`),
or version numbers can be tested against any given comparison operator.

Along with version comparison, the library also features other useful tools.

For example: version numbers can also be parsed to inspect a version number by it's bare *parts* if desired.

Inspired by PHP's [version_compare()](http://php.net/manual/en/function.version-compare.php).

- Compare two version numbers, get: `<`,`==`or`>`.
- Compare two version numbers against any comparison operator.
- Parse complex version numbers.
- Static, single-statement methods available.

# version-compare 0.0.1 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/version-compare/0.0.1

# Rust library: version-compare

A Rust library to easily compare version numbers, and test them against various comparison operators.

Comparing version numbers is hard. Especially when version numbers get really complex, or when their formatting differs.

This library helps you to easily compare any kind of version number with a single code-statement.
Two version numbers can be compared to each other, to get a relevant comparison operator (`<`, `==`, `>`),
or version numbers can be tested against any given comparison operator.

Along with version comparison, the library also features other useful tools.

For example: version numbers can also be parsed to inspect a version number by it's bare *parts* if desired.

Inspired by PHP's [version_compare()](http://php.net/manual/en/function.version-compare.php).

Note: This library is still a work in progress. See the list below for a list of currently available and future features.

## Features

- Compare two version numbers, get: `<`,`==`or`>`.
- Compare two version numbers against any comparison operator.
- Parse complex version numbers.
- Static, single-statement methods available.

The following features will be added in a later version:

- Version manifest, to specify detailed version number constraints.
- Batch comparisons.

## Usage

This library is very easy to use. Here's a basic usage example:

```
// Define some version numbers
let a = "1.2";
let b = "1.5.1";
// The following comparison operators are used:
// - CompOp::Eq -> Equal
// - CompOp::Ne -> Not equal
// - CompOp::Lt -> Less than
// - CompOp::Le -> Less than or equal
// - CompOp::Ge -> Greater than or equal
// - CompOp::Gt -> Greater than
// Easily compare
compare; // -> CompOp::Lt
compare_to; // -> true
compare_to; // -> false
// Version string parsing
let a_ver = from.unwrap;
let b_ver = from.unwrap;
// Directly compare versions
a_ver.compare; // -> CompOp::Lt
b_ver.compare; // -> CompOp::Gt
a_ver.compare_to; // -> true
// Match
match a_ver.compare
```
## Builds

This library is automatically build and tested for each commit using CI services.

| Service | Branch | Build Status | |
|---|---|---|---|
| Travis CI | master | [View Status](https://travis-ci.org/timvisee/version-compare) | |
| Travis CI | last commit | [View Status](https://travis-ci.org/timvisee/version-compare) |

## License

This project is released under the GNU GPL-3.0 license. Check out the [LICENSE](https://docs.rs/LICENSE) file for more information.

# version_compare - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/version-compare

## Expand description

Rust library to easily compare version numbers with no specific format, and test against various comparison operators.

Comparing version numbers is hard, especially with weird version number formats.

This library helps you to easily compare any kind of version number with no
specific format using a best-effort approach.
Two version numbers can be compared to each other to get a comparison operator
(`<`, `==`, `>`), or test them against a comparison operator.

Along with version comparison, the library provides various other tools for working with version numbers.

Inspired by PHPs [version_compare()](http://php.net/manual/en/function.version-compare.php).

[§](https://docs.rs#formats)Formats

Version numbers that would parse successfully include:

`1`, `3.10.4.1`, `1.2.alpha`, `1.2.dev.4`, ` `, ` .   -32 . 1`, `MyApp 3.2.0 / build 0932` …

See a list of how version numbers compare [here](https://github.com/timvisee/version-compare/blob/411ed7135741ed7cf2fcf4919012fb5412dc122b/src/test.rs#L50-L103).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use version_compare::{compare, compare_to, Cmp, Version};
let a = "1.2";
let b = "1.5.1";
// The following comparison operators are used:
// - Cmp::Eq -> Equal
// - Cmp::Ne -> Not equal
// - Cmp::Lt -> Less than
// - Cmp::Le -> Less than or equal
// - Cmp::Ge -> Greater than or equal
// - Cmp::Gt -> Greater than
// Easily compare version strings
assert_eq!(compare(a, b), Ok(Cmp::Lt));
assert_eq!(compare_to(a, b, Cmp::Le), Ok(true));
assert_eq!(compare_to(a, b, Cmp::Gt), Ok(false));
// Parse and wrap version strings as a Version
let a = Version::from(a).unwrap();
let b = Version::from(b).unwrap();
// The Version can easily be compared with
assert_eq!(a < b, true);
assert_eq!(a <= b, true);
assert_eq!(a > b, false);
assert_eq!(a != b, true);
assert_eq!(a.compare(&b), Cmp::Lt);
assert_eq!(a.compare_to(&b, Cmp::Lt), true);
// Or match the comparison operators
match a.compare(b) {
    Cmp::Lt => println!("Version a is less than b"),
    Cmp::Eq => println!("Version a is equal to b"),
    Cmp::Gt => println!("Version a is greater than b"),
    _ => unreachable!(),
}
```
See the [ examples](https://github.com/timvisee/version-compare/tree/master/examples) directory for more.

[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

- Compare version numbers, get: `<`,`==`,`>`
- Compare against a comparison operator
(`<`,`<=`,`==`,`!=`,`>=`,`>`)
- Parse complex and unspecified formats
- Static, standalone methods to easily compare version strings in a single line of code

[§](https://docs.rs#semver)Semver

Version numbers using the [semver](http://semver.org/) format are compared
correctly with no additional configuration.

If your version number strings follow this exact format you may be better off
using the [ semver](https://crates.io/crates/semver) crate for more format
specific features.

If that isn’t certain however, `version-compare` makes comparing a breeze.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Manifest](https://docs.rs/struct.Manifest.html)
- Version manifest (configuration).
- [Version](https://docs.rs/struct.Version.html)
- Version struct, wrapping a string, providing useful comparison functions.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [compare](https://docs.rs/fn.compare.html)
- Compare two version number strings to each other.
- [compare_](https://docs.rs/fn.compare_to.html)- to
- Compare two version number strings to each other and test against the given comparison
`operator`.

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/version-compare/latest/target-redirect/version_compare/index.html

## Expand description

Rust library to easily compare version numbers with no specific format, and test against various comparison operators.

This library helps you to easily compare any kind of version number with no

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```

let a = "1.2";

// - Cmp::Eq -> Equal
// - Cmp::Ne -> Not equal

[6](https://docs.rs#6)//! specific format using a best-effort approach.
[7](https://docs.rs#7)//! Two version numbers can be compared to each other to get a comparison operator
[8](https://docs.rs#8)//! (`<`, `==`, `>`), or test them against a comparison operator.
[9](https://docs.rs#9)//!

[11](https://docs.rs#11)//! working with version numbers.
[12](https://docs.rs#12)//!

[14](https://docs.rs#14)//!

[16](https://docs.rs#16)//!
[17](https://docs.rs#17)//! Version numbers that would parse successfully include:
[18](https://docs.rs#18)//! `1`, `3.10.4.1`, `1.2.alpha`, `1.2.dev.4`, ` `, ` .   -32 . 1`, `MyApp 3.2.0 / build 0932` ...
[19](https://docs.rs#19)//!
[20](https://docs.rs#20)//! See a list of how version numbers compare [here](https://github.com/timvisee/version-compare/blob/411ed7135741ed7cf2fcf4919012fb5412dc122b/src/test.rs#L50-L103).
[21](https://docs.rs#21)//!
[22](https://docs.rs#22)//! ## Examples
[23](https://docs.rs#23)//!

[25](https://docs.rs#25)//! ```rust

# version_compare - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/version-compare/latest/target-redirect/version_compare/examples/example.rs

## Expand description

Rust library to easily compare version numbers with no specific format, and test against various comparison operators.

Comparing version numbers is hard, especially with weird version number formats.

This library helps you to easily compare any kind of version number with no
specific format using a best-effort approach.
Two version numbers can be compared to each other to get a comparison operator
(`<`, `==`, `>`), or test them against a comparison operator.

Along with version comparison, the library provides various other tools for working with version numbers.

Inspired by PHPs [version_compare()](http://php.net/manual/en/function.version-compare.php).

[§](https://docs.rs#formats)Formats

Version numbers that would parse successfully include:

`1`, `3.10.4.1`, `1.2.alpha`, `1.2.dev.4`, ` `, ` .   -32 . 1`, `MyApp 3.2.0 / build 0932` …

See a list of how version numbers compare [here](https://github.com/timvisee/version-compare/blob/411ed7135741ed7cf2fcf4919012fb5412dc122b/src/test.rs#L50-L103).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use version_compare::{compare, compare_to, Cmp, Version};
let a = "1.2";
let b = "1.5.1";
// The following comparison operators are used:
// - Cmp::Eq -> Equal
// - Cmp::Ne -> Not equal
// - Cmp::Lt -> Less than
// - Cmp::Le -> Less than or equal
// - Cmp::Ge -> Greater than or equal
// - Cmp::Gt -> Greater than
// Easily compare version strings
assert_eq!(compare(a, b), Ok(Cmp::Lt));
assert_eq!(compare_to(a, b, Cmp::Le), Ok(true));
assert_eq!(compare_to(a, b, Cmp::Gt), Ok(false));
// Parse and wrap version strings as a Version
let a = Version::from(a).unwrap();
let b = Version::from(b).unwrap();
// The Version can easily be compared with
assert_eq!(a < b, true);
assert_eq!(a <= b, true);
assert_eq!(a > b, false);
assert_eq!(a != b, true);
assert_eq!(a.compare(&b), Cmp::Lt);
assert_eq!(a.compare_to(&b, Cmp::Lt), true);
// Or match the comparison operators
match a.compare(b) {
    Cmp::Lt => println!("Version a is less than b"),
    Cmp::Eq => println!("Version a is equal to b"),
    Cmp::Gt => println!("Version a is greater than b"),
    _ => unreachable!(),
}
```
See the [ examples](https://github.com/timvisee/version-compare/tree/master/examples) directory for more.

[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

- Compare version numbers, get: `<`,`==`,`>`
- Compare against a comparison operator
(`<`,`<=`,`==`,`!=`,`>=`,`>`)
- Parse complex and unspecified formats
- Static, standalone methods to easily compare version strings in a single line of code

[§](https://docs.rs#semver)Semver

Version numbers using the [semver](http://semver.org/) format are compared
correctly with no additional configuration.

If your version number strings follow this exact format you may be better off
using the [ semver](https://crates.io/crates/semver) crate for more format
specific features.

If that isn’t certain however, `version-compare` makes comparing a breeze.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Manifest](https://docs.rs/struct.Manifest.html)
- Version manifest (configuration).
- [Version](https://docs.rs/struct.Version.html)
- Version struct, wrapping a string, providing useful comparison functions.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [compare](https://docs.rs/fn.compare.html)
- Compare two version number strings to each other.
- [compare_](https://docs.rs/fn.compare_to.html)- to
- Compare two version number strings to each other and test against the given comparison
`operator`.

# Manifest in version_compare - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/version-compare/latest/target-redirect/version_compare/struct.Manifest.html

```
#[non_exhaustive]pub struct Manifest {
    pub max_depth:
```
[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)>,
    pub ignore_text: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html),
    pub gnu_ordering: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html),
}## Expand description

Version manifest (configuration).

A manifest (configuration) that is used respectively when parsing and comparing version strings.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use version_compare::{Manifest, Version};
// Create manifest with max depth of 2
let mut manifest = Manifest::default();
manifest.max_depth = Some(2);
// Version strings equal with manifest because we compare up-to 2 parts deep
let a = Version::from_manifest("1.0.1", &manifest).unwrap();
let b = Version::from_manifest("1.0.2", &manifest).unwrap();
assert!(a == b);
```
## Fields (Non-exhaustive)[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

## This struct is marked as non-exhaustive

`Struct { .. }` syntax; cannot be matched against without a wildcard `..`; and struct update syntax will not work.[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.max_depth)

`max_depth: `[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)>The maximum depth of a version number.

This specifies the maximum number of parts. There is no limit if `None` is set.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.ignore_text)

`ignore_text: `[bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)Whether to ignore text parts in version strings.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.gnu_ordering)

`gnu_ordering: `[bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)Use GNU sort based ordering.

Enabling this modifies the ordering of numbers with a leading zero to mimick GNUs sort.

Issue: https://github.com/timvisee/version-compare/issues/27

# Version in version_compare - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/version-compare/latest/target-redirect/version_compare/struct.Version.html

`pub struct Version<'a> { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Version struct, wrapping a string, providing useful comparison functions.

A version in string format can be parsed using methods like `Version::from("1.2.3");`,
returning a `Result` with the parse result.

The original version string can be accessed using `version.as_str()`. A `Version` that isn’t
derrived from a version string returns a generated string.

The struct provides many methods for easy comparison and probing.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use version_compare::{Version};
let ver = Version::from("1.2.3").unwrap();
```
## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Create a `Version` instance from a version string.

The version string should be passed to the `version` parameter.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-1)Examples

```
use version_compare::{Cmp, Version};
let a = Version::from("1.2.3").unwrap();
let b = Version::from("1.3.0").unwrap();
assert_eq!(a.compare(b), Cmp::Lt);
```

Create a `Version` instance from a version string with the given `manifest`.

The version string should be passed to the `version` parameter.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-3)Examples

```
use version_compare::{Cmp, Version, Manifest};
let manifest = Manifest::default();
let ver = Version::from_manifest("1.2.3", &manifest).unwrap();
assert_eq!(ver.compare(Version::from("1.2.3").unwrap()), Cmp::Eq);
```
Get the version manifest, if available.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-4)Examples

```
use version_compare::Version;
let version = Version::from("1.2.3").unwrap();
if version.has_manifest() {
    println!(
        "Maximum version part depth is {} for this version",
        version.manifest().unwrap().max_depth.unwrap_or(0),
    );
} else {
    println!("Version has no manifest");
}
```

Get a specific version part by it’s `index`.
An error is returned if the given index is out of bound.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-8)Examples

```
use version_compare::{Version, Part};
let ver = Version::from("1.2.3").unwrap();
assert_eq!(ver.part(0), Ok(Part::Number(1)));
assert_eq!(ver.part(1), Ok(Part::Number(2)));
assert_eq!(ver.part(2), Ok(Part::Number(3)));
```
Get a vector of all version parts.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-9)Examples

```
use version_compare::{Version, Part};
let ver = Version::from("1.2.3").unwrap();
assert_eq!(ver.parts(), [
    Part::Number(1),
    Part::Number(2),
    Part::Number(3)
]);
```
Compare this version to the given `other` version using the default `Manifest`.

This method returns one of the following comparison operators:

- `Lt`
- `Eq`
- `Gt`

Other comparison operators can be used when comparing, but aren’t returned by this method.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-10)Examples:

```
use version_compare::{Cmp, Version};
let a = Version::from("1.2").unwrap();
let b = Version::from("1.3.2").unwrap();
assert_eq!(a.compare(&b), Cmp::Lt);
assert_eq!(b.compare(&a), Cmp::Gt);
assert_eq!(a.compare(&a), Cmp::Eq);
```
```

20    // - Cmp::Le -> Less than or equal

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/version_compare/version.rs.html#270-280)#### pub fn [compare_to](https://docs.rs#method.compare_to)<V>(&self, other: V, operator: [Cmp](https://docs.rs/enum.Cmp.html)) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/version_compare/version.rs.html#270-280)

#### pub fn [compare_to](https://docs.rs#method.compare_to)<V>(&self, other: V, operator: [Cmp](https://docs.rs/enum.Cmp.html)) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

Compare this version to the given `other` version,
and check whether the given comparison operator is valid using the default `Manifest`.

All comparison operators can be used.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-11)Examples:

```

assert!(a.compare_to(&b, Cmp::Le));
assert!(a.compare_to(&a, Cmp::Eq));
assert!(a.compare_to(&a, Cmp::Le));
```

48}
```

# Cmp in version_compare - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/version-compare/latest/target-redirect/version_compare/enum.Cmp.html

```
pub enum Cmp {
    Eq,
    Ne,
    Lt,
    Le,
    Ge,
    Gt,
}
```
## Expand description

Comparison operators enum.

## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Eq)

### Eq

Equal (`==`, `=`).
When version `A` is equal to `B`.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Ne)

### Ne

Not equal (`!=`, `!`, `<>`).
When version `A` is not equal to `B`.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Lt)

### Lt

Less than (`<`).
When version `A` is less than `B` but not equal.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Le)

### Le

Less or equal (`<=`).
When version `A` is less than or equal to `B`.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Ge)

### Ge

Greater or equal (`>=`).
When version `A` is greater than or equal to `B`.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Gt)

### Gt

Greater than (`>`).
When version `A` is greater than `B` but not equal.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Get a comparison operator by it’s sign. Whitespaces are stripped from the sign string. An error is returned if the sign isn’t recognized.

The following signs are supported:

- `==`- *or*- `=`->- `Eq`
- `!=`- *or*- `!`- *or*- `<>`->- `Ne`
- `<`->- `Lt`
- `<=`->- `Le`
- `>=`->- `Ge`
- `>`->- `Gt`

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use version_compare::Cmp;
assert_eq!(Cmp::from_sign("=="), Ok(Cmp::Eq));
assert_eq!(Cmp::from_sign("<"), Ok(Cmp::Lt));
assert_eq!(Cmp::from_sign("  >=   "), Ok(Cmp::Ge));
assert!(Cmp::from_sign("*").is_err());
```
Get a comparison operator by it’s name. Names are case-insensitive, and whitespaces are stripped from the string. An error is returned if the name isn’t recognized.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-1)Examples

```
use version_compare::Cmp;
assert_eq!(Cmp::from_name("eq"), Ok(Cmp::Eq));
assert_eq!(Cmp::from_name("lt"), Ok(Cmp::Lt));
assert_eq!(Cmp::from_name("  Ge   "), Ok(Cmp::Ge));
assert!(Cmp::from_name("abc").is_err());
```
Get the comparison operator from Rusts `Ordering` enum.

The following comparison operators are returned:

- `Ordering::Less`->- `Lt`
- `Ordering::Equal`->- `Eq`
- `Ordering::Greater`->- `Gt`

Get the inverted comparison operator.

This uses the following bidirectional rules:

- `Eq`<->- `Ne`
- `Lt`<->- `Ge`
- `Le`<->- `Gt`

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-3)Examples

```
use version_compare::Cmp;
assert_eq!(Cmp::Eq.invert(), Cmp::Ne);
assert_eq!(Cmp::Lt.invert(), Cmp::Ge);
assert_eq!(Cmp::Gt.invert(), Cmp::Le);
```
Get the opposite comparison operator.

This uses the following bidirectional rules:

- `Eq`<->- `Ne`
- `Lt`<->- `Gt`
- `Le`<->- `Ge`

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-4)Examples

```
use version_compare::Cmp;
assert_eq!(Cmp::Eq.opposite(), Cmp::Ne);
assert_eq!(Cmp::Lt.opposite(), Cmp::Gt);
assert_eq!(Cmp::Ge.opposite(), Cmp::Le);
```
Get the flipped comparison operator.

This uses the following bidirectional rules:

- `Lt`<->- `Gt`
- `Le`<->- `Ge`
- Other operators are returned as is.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-5)Examples

```
use version_compare::Cmp;
assert_eq!(Cmp::Eq.flip(), Cmp::Eq);
assert_eq!(Cmp::Lt.flip(), Cmp::Gt);
assert_eq!(Cmp::Ge.flip(), Cmp::Le);
```
Get the sign for this comparison operator.

The following signs are returned:

- `Eq`->- `==`
- `Ne`->- `!=`
- `Lt`->- `<`
- `Le`->- `<=`
- `Ge`->- `>=`
- `Gt`->- `>`

Note: Some comparison operators also support other signs,
such as `=` for `Eq` and `!` for `Ne`,
these are never returned by this method however as the table above is used.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-6)Examples

```
use version_compare::Cmp;
assert_eq!(Cmp::Eq.sign(), "==");
assert_eq!(Cmp::Lt.sign(), "<");
assert_eq!(Cmp::Ge.flip().sign(), "<=");
```
Get a factor (number) for this comparison operator. These factors can be useful for quick calculations.

The following factor numbers are returned:

- `Eq`- *or*- `Ne`->- `0`
- `Lt`- *or*- `Le`->- `-1`
- `Gt`- *or*- `Ge`->- `1`

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-7)Examples

```
use version_compare::Version;
let a = Version::from("1.2.3").unwrap();
let b = Version::from("1.3").unwrap();
assert_eq!(a.compare(&b).factor(), -1);
assert_eq!(10 * b.compare(a).factor(), 10);
```
Get Rust’s ordering for this comparison operator.

The following comparison operators are supported:

- `Eq`->- `Ordering::Equal`
- `Lt`->- `Ordering::Less`
- `Gt`->- `Ordering::Greater`

For other comparison operators `None` is returned.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-8)Examples

```
use std::cmp::Ordering;
use version_compare::Version;
let a = Version::from("1.2.3").unwrap();
let b = Version::from("1.3").unwrap();
assert_eq!(a.compare(b).ord().unwrap(), Ordering::Less);
```

# compare in version_compare - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/version-compare/latest/target-redirect/version_compare/fn.compare.html

## Expand description

Compare two version number strings to each other.

This compares version `a` to version `b`, and returns whether version `a` is greater, less
or equal to version `b`.

If either version number string is invalid an error is returned.

One of the following operators is returned:

- `Cmp::Eq`
- `Cmp::Lt`
- `Cmp::Gt`

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use version_compare::{Cmp, compare};
assert_eq!(compare("1.2.3", "1.2.3"), Ok(Cmp::Eq));
assert_eq!(compare("1.2.3", "1.2.4"), Ok(Cmp::Lt));
assert_eq!(compare("1", "0.1"), Ok(Cmp::Gt));
```
## More examples

```
12fn main() {
13    let a = "1.2";
14    let b = "1.5.1";
15
16    // The following comparison operators are used:
17    // - Cmp::Eq -> Equal
18    // - Cmp::Ne -> Not equal
19    // - Cmp::Lt -> Less than
20    // - Cmp::Le -> Less than or equal
21    // - Cmp::Ge -> Greater than or equal
22    // - Cmp::Gt -> Greater than
23
24    // Easily compare version strings
25    assert_eq!(compare(a, b), Ok(Cmp::Lt));
26    assert_eq!(compare_to(a, b, Cmp::Le), Ok(true));
27    assert_eq!(compare_to(a, b, Cmp::Gt), Ok(false));
28
29    // Parse and wrap version strings as a Version
30    let a = Version::from(a).unwrap();
31    let b = Version::from(b).unwrap();
32
33    // The Version can easily be compared with
34    assert_eq!(a < b, true);
35    assert_eq!(a <= b, true);
36    assert_eq!(a > b, false);
37    assert_eq!(a != b, true);
38    assert_eq!(a.compare(&b), Cmp::Lt);
39    assert_eq!(a.compare_to(&b, Cmp::Lt), true);
40
41    // Or match the comparison operators
42    match a.compare(b) {
43        Cmp::Lt => println!("Version a is less than b"),
44        Cmp::Eq => println!("Version a is equal to b"),
45        Cmp::Gt => println!("Version a is greater than b"),
46        _ => unreachable!(),
47    }
48}
```

---

# compare_to in version_compare - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/version-compare/latest/target-redirect/version_compare/fn.compare_to.html

## Expand description

Compare two version number strings to each other and test against the given comparison
`operator`.

If either version number string is invalid an error is returned.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use version_compare::{Cmp, compare_to};
assert!(compare_to("1.2.3", "1.2.3", Cmp::Eq).unwrap());
assert!(compare_to("1.2.3", "1.2.3", Cmp::Le).unwrap());
assert!(compare_to("1.2.3", "1.2.4", Cmp::Lt).unwrap());
assert!(compare_to("1", "0.1", Cmp::Gt).unwrap());
assert!(compare_to("1", "0.1", Cmp::Ge).unwrap());
```
```
12fn main() {
13    let a = "1.2";
14    let b = "1.5.1";
15
16    // The following comparison operators are used:
17    // - Cmp::Eq -> Equal
18    // - Cmp::Ne -> Not equal
19    // - Cmp::Lt -> Less than
20    // - Cmp::Le -> Less than or equal
21    // - Cmp::Ge -> Greater than or equal
22    // - Cmp::Gt -> Greater than
23
24    // Easily compare version strings
25    assert_eq!(compare(a, b), Ok(Cmp::Lt));
26    assert_eq!(compare_to(a, b, Cmp::Le), Ok(true));
27    assert_eq!(compare_to(a, b, Cmp::Gt), Ok(false));
28
29    // Parse and wrap version strings as a Version
30    let a = Version::from(a).unwrap();
31    let b = Version::from(b).unwrap();
32
33    // The Version can easily be compared with
34    assert_eq!(a < b, true);
35    assert_eq!(a <= b, true);
36    assert_eq!(a > b, false);
37    assert_eq!(a != b, true);
38    assert_eq!(a.compare(&b), Cmp::Lt);
39    assert_eq!(a.compare_to(&b, Cmp::Lt), true);
40
41    // Or match the comparison operators
42    match a.compare(b) {
43        Cmp::Lt => println!("Version a is less than b"),
44        Cmp::Eq => println!("Version a is equal to b"),
45        Cmp::Gt => println!("Version a is greater than b"),
46        _ => unreachable!(),
47    }
48}
```

# clap - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/clap

## Expand description

Command Line Argument Parser for Rust

Quick Links:

- Derive [tutorial](https://docs.rs/_derive/_tutorial/index.html)and[reference](https://docs.rs/_derive/index.html)
- Builder [tutorial](https://docs.rs/_tutorial/index.html)and[reference](https://docs.rs/struct.Command.html)
- [Cookbook](https://docs.rs/_cookbook/index.html)
- [CLI Concepts](https://docs.rs/_concepts/index.html)
- [FAQ](https://docs.rs/_faq/index.html)
- [Discussions](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/discussions)
- [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/blob/v4.6.1/CHANGELOG.md)(includes major version migration guides)

[§](https://docs.rs#aspirations)Aspirations

- Out of the box, users get a polished CLI experience
- Including common argument behavior, help generation, suggested fixes for users, colored output, [shell completions](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/tree/master/clap_complete), etc

- Including common argument behavior, help generation, suggested fixes for users, colored output,
- Flexible enough to port your existing CLI interface
- However, we won’t necessarily streamline support for each use case

- Reasonable parse performance
- Resilient maintainership, including
- Willing to break compatibility rather than batching up breaking changes in large releases
- Leverage feature flags to keep to one active branch
- Being under [WG-CLI](https://github.com/rust-cli/team/)to increase the bus factor

- We follow semver and will wait about 6-9 months between major breaking changes
- We will support the last two minor Rust releases (MSRV, currently 1.74)

While these aspirations can be at odds with fast build times and low binary
size, we will still strive to keep these reasonable for the flexibility you
get.  Check out the
[argparse-benchmarks](https://github.com/rust-cli/argparse-benchmarks-rs) for
CLI parsers optimized for other use cases.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

Run

`$ cargo add clap --features derive`*(See also  feature flag reference)*

Then define your CLI in `main.rs`:

```
use clap::Parser;
/// Simple program to greet a person
#[derive(Parser, Debug)]
#[command(version, about, long_about = None)]
struct Args {
    /// Name of the person to greet
    #[arg(short, long)]
    name: String,
    /// Number of times to greet
    #[arg(short, long, default_value_t = 1)]
    count: u8,
}
fn main() {
    let args = Args::parse();
    for _ in 0..args.count {
        println!("Hello {}!", args.name);
    }
}
```
And try it out:

```
$ demo --help
A simple to use, efficient, and full-featured Command Line Argument Parser
Usage: demo[EXE] [OPTIONS] --name <NAME>
Options:
  -n, --name <NAME>    Name of the person to greet
  -c, --count <COUNT>  Number of times to greet [default: 1]
  -h, --help           Print help
  -V, --version        Print version
$ demo --name Me
Hello Me!
```
*(version number and  .exe extension on windows replaced by placeholders)*

See also the derive [tutorial](https://docs.rs/_derive/_tutorial/index.html) and [reference](https://docs.rs/_derive/index.html)

[§](https://docs.rs#related-projects)Related Projects

Augment clap:

- [wild](https://crates.io/crates/wild)for supporting wildcards (- `*`) on Windows like you do Linux
- [argfile](https://crates.io/crates/argfile)for loading additional arguments from a file (aka response files)
- [shadow-rs](https://crates.io/crates/shadow-rs)for generating- `Command::long_version`
- [clap_mangen](https://crates.io/crates/clap_mangen)for generating man page source (roff)
- [clap_complete](https://crates.io/crates/clap_complete)for shell completion support
- [clap-i18n-richformatter](https://crates.io/crates/clap-i18n-richformatter)for i18n support with- `clap::error::RichFormatter`

CLI Helpers

- [clio](https://crates.io/crates/clio)for reading/writing to files specified as arguments
- [clap-verbosity-flag](https://crates.io/crates/clap-verbosity-flag)
- [clap-cargo](https://crates.io/crates/clap-cargo)
- [colorchoice-clap](https://crates.io/crates/colorchoice-clap)

Testing

- `trycmd`
- `snapbox`
- `assert_cmd`- `assert_fs`

Documentation:

# clap - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/clap::Command

## Expand description

Command Line Argument Parser for Rust

Quick Links:

- Derive [tutorial](https://docs.rs/_derive/_tutorial/index.html)and[reference](https://docs.rs/_derive/index.html)
- Builder [tutorial](https://docs.rs/_tutorial/index.html)and[reference](https://docs.rs/struct.Command.html)

- [FAQ](https://docs.rs/_faq/index.html)
- [Discussions](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/discussions)
- [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/blob/v4.6.1/CHANGELOG.md)(includes major version migration guides)

[§](https://docs.rs#aspirations)Aspirations

- Out of the box, users get a polished CLI experience
- Including common argument behavior, help generation, suggested fixes for users, colored output, [shell completions](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/tree/master/clap_complete), etc

- Including common argument behavior, help generation, suggested fixes for users, colored output,
- Flexible enough to port your existing CLI interface
- However, we won’t necessarily streamline support for each use case

- Reasonable parse performance
- Resilient maintainership, including
- Willing to break compatibility rather than batching up breaking changes in large releases
- Leverage feature flags to keep to one active branch
- Being under [WG-CLI](https://github.com/rust-cli/team/)to increase the bus factor

- We follow semver and will wait about 6-9 months between major breaking changes
- We will support the last two minor Rust releases (MSRV, currently 1.74)

While these aspirations can be at odds with fast build times and low binary
size, we will still strive to keep these reasonable for the flexibility you
get.  Check out the
[argparse-benchmarks](https://github.com/rust-cli/argparse-benchmarks-rs) for
CLI parsers optimized for other use cases.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

Run

`$ cargo add clap --features derive`*(See also  feature flag reference)*

Then define your CLI in `main.rs`:

```
use clap::Parser;
/// Simple program to greet a person
#[derive(Parser, Debug)]
#[command(version, about, long_about = None)]
struct Args {
    /// Name of the person to greet
    #[arg(short, long)]
    name: String,
    /// Number of times to greet
    #[arg(short, long, default_value_t = 1)]
    count: u8,
}
fn main() {
    let args = Args::parse();
    for _ in 0..args.count {
        println!("Hello {}!", args.name);
    }
}
```
And try it out:

```
$ demo --help
A simple to use, efficient, and full-featured Command Line Argument Parser
Usage: demo[EXE] [OPTIONS] --name <NAME>
Options:
  -n, --name <NAME>    Name of the person to greet
  -c, --count <COUNT>  Number of times to greet [default: 1]
  -h, --help           Print help
  -V, --version        Print version
$ demo --name Me
Hello Me!
```
*(version number and  .exe extension on windows replaced by placeholders)*

See also the derive [tutorial](https://docs.rs/_derive/_tutorial/index.html) and [reference](https://docs.rs/_derive/index.html)
